verdict: Read only against its own objective, principles and S1 to S11, the spec does not yet meet them: S1 cannot be produced under the 10 10.2 workflow grammar, the objective's two absolute sentences (nothing lost, nothing agent-written executed on the host) are wider than the mechanisms behind them and have no restore journey and no build-location measurement, and the merge gate is a convention stated as enforcement in four places that carry two states of one fact.

findings.defect: The workflow grammar forbids every permission value other than read or none, every secrets.<name> and github.token, and persist-credentials, while the same section's release.yml must attest (id-token and attestations write), create a release (contents write plus a token for gh), verify attestations with gh and upload dora.json, so no release.yml that satisfies S1 can pass tools/ci workflows.
findings.scenario: T088 writes release.yml as 10 10.2 describes; tools/ci workflows fails it on permissions and on the token gh needs; the author widens the grammar in the same PR under an approval line they typed; S1 ships from a grammar nobody designed.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 state the exact exception for release.yml: the job-level permissions it may hold (id-token: write, attestations: write, contents: write), the one way gh receives a token (a named variable the grammar lists for that file alone), and that tools/ci workflows admits those only in .github/workflows/release.yml; say which 'run' steps may use it. Update 12 12.10 (--attach) and S1's evidence to match.
findings.cost: a paragraph and a grammar rule with a fixture; a decision on how the release token is scoped

findings.defect: The Release signing paragraph and ADR 0008 decision 6 fix a credential that signs release artifacts, held outside GitHub as an operator step, and S1, J1 step 2, 10 10.2 Release and bootstrap and tools/release name no artifact it signs and no step that verifies it.
findings.scenario: v1.0.0 is released with checksums.txt and attestations; the operator never signs anything because no step asks; a reader of 05 5.4 believes releases carry an operator signature and verifies against nothing.
findings.change: Either add the signed artifact to S1 (what is signed, with which tool, how J1 verifies it, which tools/release subcommand checks it) or rewrite the paragraph to say that in v1 the keyless attestation is the only signature and the operator credential is deferred with a trigger.
findings.cost: a decision by the maintainer; then either a task or four sentences

findings.defect: The objective says nothing sandbox-only is lost on recreate or removal, while 08 8.5 salvages a closed list (repos, ignored files under a cap minus excludes, agent memory files and todos, transcripts on request) and nothing lists what is left behind by design.
findings.scenario: An agent keeps notes under $HOME outside any repo, installs a plugin, has herdr scrollback and julieta state; the operator runs romeu rm; salvage reports complete; those are gone and nothing said they would be.
findings.change: Qualify the objective bullet ('nothing sandbox-only that salvage covers, 08 8.5') and add to 08 8.5 one table of what salvage does not take, cited from 00 0.1 and 05 5.4.

findings.defect: Salvage proves preservation and no page says how work is recovered into a new sandbox: salvage refs live under refs/romeu/salvage on the host clone, which a clone-mode create does not copy, the dirty-tree commit and stashes are ULID-named refs, and ignored.tar.gz has no verb to unpack it.
findings.scenario: The operator runs romeu recreate after a kit bump; the new sandbox has none of the uncommitted work; J6 ends at 'continue with J3b'; the only path is J10 step 3, raw git on the host clone, which 05 5.4 row 1 lists as a residual risk.
findings.change: Add a restore step to J6 (or a journey) and the verb or the documented hardened commands that bring salvage refs, stashes and ignored.tar.gz back into the sandbox; say in 08 8.5 that recovery is the operator's and how.
findings.cost: a journey plus either a julieta verb (a task) or a documented manual path

findings.defect: Step 4 tars every ignored file not in salvage.excludeIgnored into the host memory dir; .gitignore is where .env files and local credentials live, and 05 5.4 has a row for a secret in the ledger and none for a secret in that tarball.
findings.scenario: A repo has .env with a provider key; the spec lists node_modules/ only; romeu rm writes ignored.tar.gz into memory/<dir>/salvage and the host backup takes it; the key now lives in two more places.
findings.change: Add a 05 5.4 row, and in 08 8.5 either a default exclude pattern set or a required acknowledgement in the gate diff that lists the ignored patterns that will be salvaged.
findings.cost: a row and a decision on a default exclude list

findings.defect: The objective says nothing an agent wrote is ever executed on the host, personal kits are agent-authored (01 1.2, 06 6.1) and sbx builds them at create, and no probe records whether BuildKit runs a local kit's install steps on the host engine or inside the microVM.
findings.scenario: A personal kit install step runs on the host's Docker engine at sbx env run; the gate showed the diff and the operator approved it, so it is reviewed, which is a weaker claim than the one written.
findings.change: Add the measurement to A11 or A14 (where does an install step execute, as the harness can observe) and make the objective's sentence match what is measured, or add 'unreviewed' to it.
findings.cost: one probe observation and one word

findings.defect: How romeu run reaches the run layout treats an absent and a present sandbox and never a present, stopped one; 09 J3a says sbx env run -d starts or reattaches, 01 1.6 has no event for it, and no block A probe runs sbx env run -d or sbx env exec on a stopped sandbox (A4 stops and lists only).
findings.scenario: The operator closes the laptop, sbx stops the sandbox, romeu run the next morning either calls env run -d on a stopped sandbox or execs into one; which, and whether it works, is written in a journey sentence and measured nowhere; the fake sbx replays a shape nobody recorded.
findings.change: In 04 run step 3 say what run does when the sandbox is present and stopped; add the restart to A4's steps; add the stopped case to romeu stop's row.
findings.cost: two sentences and one probe step

findings.defect: Step 5 exits 2 for every P command of a project using git-ssh-sign when the signing socket is unset, unreachable or holds the wrong keys, salvage, rm and salvage --from-host included, so a host check that cannot widen a sandbox blocks the commands whose job is to preserve data.
findings.scenario: After a reboot the dedicated agent is not running; the sandbox is dying; romeu salvage --from-host exits 2 with RJ-204 until the operator restarts an ssh-agent.
findings.change: Exempt salvage, rm and retire from the signing row of step 5 (they forward no socket), or say why the refusal protects data; keep it for run, sync, stop and pull.
findings.cost: one sentence and one table cell

findings.defect: The approval-line row, 10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4's merge row and 12 12.9 each state that the default-branch ruleset requires a code-owner review and, in the same cell or paragraph, that as measured on 2026-10-08 it requires none; the spec describes current state only (12 12.5) and carries two states of one fact in four places.
findings.scenario: An implementer of tools/ci pr or the author of CONTRIBUTING.md reads one half and builds or documents a review step that does not exist; a security reader trusts the first half.
findings.change: State the ruleset's current requirements once, in 05 5.4, as measured; make the other three places point there; move the earlier configuration to reviews/ or ADR 0008.
findings.cost: edits to four places, no decision

findings.defect: The row 'main is releasable at every merge' names the default-branch ruleset as what enforces 'no merge without the full list green', while required status checks are a bootstrap item with an administrator bypass the sandbox's token holds (ADR 0008, index: Deferred decisions) and the merge itself is process only; 12 12.4's merge row lists CI green the same way.
findings.scenario: A reader of the practices table believes a red run blocks a merge; an agent with the token merges a red PR through the API; nothing refused it, and the row said something did.
findings.change: Tag the row [review] with a pointer to 05 5.4 and the deferred row, or write 'convention until the deferred row on required checks closes'.

findings.defect: Q4, Q6, Q9, Q12, Q13, Q14 and Q23 carry a bold default and 'Settled by: maintainer' with no event, and Q25 is marked decided yet kept; by ADR 0005's own distinction (a question has a way to settle it, a deferral has an event) these are decisions taken by default and waiting for a record, not open questions.
findings.scenario: A reader counts eleven open questions on the eve of the candidate and asks what is undecided; seven of them were decided in round 2 and T101 writes their ADRs in phase 9.
findings.change: Move the seven to a 'decided, record pending (T101)' list or straight to ADRs; drop Q25 from the table now that ADR 0008 exists; keep Open questions for rows a probe settles.
findings.cost: a table edit; the ADRs are already T101's

findings.defect: The row 'the review interval of the token narrowing' duplicates the interval the row above it already carries and its trigger is 'the operator saying so', which ADR 0005 rule 3 calls a feeling and not an event; the hash-chain, cross-machine-sync, stacked-PR and dark-package rows name triggers no check or person is assigned to observe.
findings.scenario: The interval row and the narrowing row drift apart on their next edit; the stacked-PR trigger (a second Lessons section that records a wait) fires and nobody counts.
findings.change: Fold the interval into the narrowing row; for each trigger that a tool could detect (dora, lessons) name the check per ADR 0005 Consequences, else name who observes.

findings.defect: The Threat model defers two escapes that act before tools/ci starts (an untracked go.work in a parent directory, GOFLAGS=-overlay) 'until the hook next changes, or until Q25 is decided' and points at a plan row 'whether agents push from a second account' that plan.md does not have; Q25 is decided by ADR 0008, so the trigger fired, and no row in the index's Deferred decisions holds the two escapes.
findings.scenario: The hook is next changed for another reason; nobody recalls the two escapes because the only record is a sentence in an accepted ADR pointing at a row that does not exist; the index's rule 'a deferral without a row is an oversight' is met by its own text.
findings.change: Add one Deferred decisions row for the two escapes with what holds until then and a live trigger (the next change to .githooks/pre-push); note in ADR 0008 Consequences that ADR 0007's trigger fired.

findings.defect: The runtime ledger (three stores, three invariants, a view policy, a probe, two commands, seven concepts by ADR 0006's count) traces to no success criterion, has no row in 00 0.5's scope table, and ADR 0006 neither argues it is a need of the start nor records a collision with ADR 0005 rule 1 the way ADR 0008 does.
findings.scenario: The spec's principle says a mechanism the start does not need is left out; the ledger is built because 'the maintainer asked'; stacked PRs and a feature flag, which the same principle deferred, had better triggers than the ledger has consumers (13 13.9: the maintainer reading JSON lines).
findings.change: Either add the ledger's row to 00 0.5 with the criterion, journey or named need it serves, and the matching exception sentence to ADR 0006; or move 13 to v1.1 with a trigger row.
findings.cost: a maintainer decision; then a row and a sentence, or a plan change

findings.defect: skills/** (the text every agent follows in every sandbox, installed by the julieta-claude kit) and internal/sbxdrv (the only code that runs sbx, holding the I4 and I25 guards) are on no ask-first surface, while kits/** and catalog/egress.yaml are; docs/spec/05-security.md is read by tools/ci acceptance for S6 and is not a surface either.
findings.scenario: A PR edits skills/julieta/SKILL.md to tell the agent to skip julieta memory, or deletes a row of 05 5.2; no approval line is required; it merges with the operator's token; every sandbox of every user follows it.
findings.change: Add surfaces for skills/** and internal/sbxdrv/** (and consider internal/render, internal/shquote, internal/salvage) and list docs/spec/05-security.md under checks or decisions.
findings.cost: four lines of YAML and the generated consumers

findings.defect: Rows 2 and 3 say 'the token is today the operator's own, not per-project (ADR 0008)' and ADR 0008 Context says the forwarded agent holds two keys, while 06 6.4 says the full host agent is never forwarded and the product's token is whatever name@project argv the operator binds (03 3.4): the residual-risk table presents the maintainer's development sandbox as a property of the product a user installs.
findings.scenario: A second adopter reads SECURITY.md and 05 5.4, concludes romeu forwards the operator's whole GitHub identity and two SSH keys into each sandbox, and does not install.
findings.change: Separate the two in 05 5.4: a short block on 'the sandbox that builds this product' pointing at ADR 0008, and rows about the product's own sandboxes that name the per-project token and the one-key agent of 06 6.4.
findings.cost: a paragraph and two cell edits

findings.defect: SessionStart prints every open memory entry and every lesson entry with no bound, the store allows 10 000 entries of 1 MiB, and the threat model of 05 does not name agent-written memory, handoff and lesson text as an injection channel into the next session.
findings.scenario: A repo's memory has 400 open entries; every session starts with megabytes in context and the agent stops reading them, which defeats 'the agent consumes memory instead of remembering'; or one planted lesson entry steers every future session of that repo.
findings.change: Cap what --hook prints (newest N, by ULID, with a count of the rest) and add a 05 threat-model sentence and a 5.4 row for agent-facing text channels (memory, handoff, others.jsonl).
findings.cost: a number, a sentence and a row

findings.defect: The end-of-plan check requires a committed result only for probes named in the index's Settled by column; A2, A3, A5, A6, A9 and A14 are named in none, and 11 11.4 says a probe nobody ran is noticed only in that table, so A3 (the probe for I24, I30, I32, I33 and the mount model) can be skipped without tools/ci acceptance noticing.
findings.scenario: Block A is run under time pressure and A3 is deferred; every later check passes; v1.0.0 is accepted with the read-only mount enforcement never observed on a real host.
findings.change: Make the acceptance rule 'every probe id of 11 has a committed result, from both hosts when arch-sensitive', and drop the Settled by dependence.

findings.defect: The consequence 'secondary repos need the project's git credential inside the sandbox' and 07 7.4's 'the project's github secret covers it' rest on a mechanism the spec never states (how a named secret resolved by a host command becomes the credential git, gh and mise present to GitHub inside the sandbox) and that no probe measures; 10 10.3 lists credential injection under Cannot model.
findings.scenario: The operator binds github@shop; the agent's git push fails or succeeds for reasons nobody in the spec can name; B3 is the first time anyone sees it, after the candidate tag.
findings.change: State the mechanism in 01 1.3 boundary B or 02 2.6 as documented sbx behavior, and add to block A a probe that pushes and calls the API from inside a sandbox with a scoped secret.

findings.defect: julieta pin workload and pin check read the container registry from inside the config project's sandbox, and the catalog's meta and base sets (03 3.5) derive no registry host, so J9's step '[A] julieta pin workload in the config sandbox' is blocked by egress unless the config spec adds the registry by hand, which no page says.
findings.scenario: The agent runs julieta pin workload projects/foo.yaml; the request to the registry is denied; the agent asks for a native approval or edits egress.extra; neither is in J9.
findings.change: Either add the workload registries (from host settings workloadRepositories) to the config project's derived egress, or write the egress.extra requirement into J9 and 02 2.2.
findings.cost: a derivation rule or two sentences

findings.defect: julieta spec validate --catalog exits 1 on a lock host missing from the catalog, while romeu's derivation (07 7.5 step 3) gates such a host and continues, so the config repo's CI is red for a case the product accepts after approval; S4 is defined on backend:tool only.
findings.scenario: A lock records a host the catalog lacks; romeu sync gates it and the operator approves; validate.yml stays red until a catalog PR, with no rule saying which tool is right.
findings.change: Make validate --catalog report lock hosts as warnings and exit 1 on unknown backend:tool only, or make 07 7.5 step 3 an error; say which in both places.

findings.defect: julieta salvage takes an optional --stop-agents, 01 1.7 defines salvage as 'stop agents, capture everything', J6 passes the flag for rm and recreate, and no row says whether a standalone romeu salvage passes it.
findings.scenario: romeu salvage kills the agent mid-session, or does not and salvages a moving tree whose secondaries have no daemon cross-check (05 5.4).
findings.change: State in the romeu salvage row which commands pass --stop-agents and the default for a standalone salvage.

findings.defect: S8 bounds romeu's own overhead with sbx time excluded and setup against local origins, and no criterion bounds or even records the end-to-end wait of romeu run warm on a real host, which is what the objective's 'opens the project's sandbox straight into its run layout' is about.
findings.scenario: S8 is green at 1.2 s while every warm run takes 40 s inside sbx and the fetch; the user experience the criterion was meant to protect is unmeasured.
findings.change: Add an observed (not gated) end-to-end figure to B5: romeu run warm wall time, median of 5, recorded in the result.

findings.defect: Every evidence item of S1 to S11 is a CI run, a probe on throwaway projects or a document; nothing requires the product to have carried the maintainer's own work for any period, so the objective (a developer's daily organizer) has no criterion that a day of use can fail.
findings.scenario: v1.0.0 passes all eleven criteria and the maintainer discovers the restart path and the restore gap in the first week of real use.
findings.change: Add a criterion: N real sessions on the candidate across M projects, with handoffs and salvage records as evidence, before the v1.0.0 tag.
findings.cost: one row and operator time already spent on the rehearsal

findings.defect: romeu.lock is one per machine and run holds it through sbx env run, so creating project a (kit builds, minutes) makes romeu run b exit 1 with RJ-101 although the two share no state.
findings.scenario: The operator starts two projects in the morning; the second refuses until the first's kits are built.
findings.change: Either a per-project lock with a short machine-wide lock for shared state (toolchain, workspace files), or one sentence that names the serialization as a chosen cost.
findings.cost: a design decision, or one sentence

findings.defect: The opening of 09 says J12 runs J1 steps 3 to 6 and the J12 section says J1 steps 1 to 5.
findings.scenario: The J12 scenario function and the J12 guide page follow different sentences.
findings.change: Make the two agree (steps 3 to 6 fits a second machine that already has sbx and romeu installed only if the install is a precondition; say which).

findings.defect: The two workspace files are rewritten whole from host state with no record of their hash, so a hand edit (a memory dir added as a folder, which boundary D forbids) is live until the next promotion or retire, and doctor has no row for it.
findings.scenario: The operator adds memory/shop-api to dev.code-workspace for convenience; VS Code opens an agent-writable tree; nothing reports it for days.
findings.change: Add a doctor row that compares the live workspace files with the derivation, or record their hashes in render.json and drift-check them.

findings.defect: The memory entry content digest is {title, body, created}; tags are outside it and memory verify compares status only, so an entry whose tags were stripped (lesson among them, the tag SessionStart keys on) verifies equal.
findings.scenario: A bulk import of pre-v1 memory loses every lesson tag; verify passes; SessionStart prints no lessons.
findings.change: Include sorted tags in the verify comparison next to status, or in the digest.

findings.defect: The opening says every format has a version field, strict decoding and a JSON Schema in schemas/; run-timings.v1 (02 2.1, 04 4.2) is defined nowhere in 03, and snapshot/heads.json, SHA256SUMS, the ledger entry and view files and dora.v1 have no schema and are not named as exceptions in 3.13.
findings.scenario: An implementer looks for run-timings.v1 in 03 and invents it; tools/ci schema has nothing to compare.
findings.change: Define run-timings.v1 in 03 and list the formats without a schema as exceptions in 3.13 with the reason.
findings.cost: a short section and a list

findings.defect: I3's E test enumerates nine romeu commands (init, sync, run, pull, salvage, rm, retire, status, doctor) and I7's E test six, while romeu has fifteen (stop, approve, adopt, handoff, recreate, ledger ingest, ledger query are absent), and the Boundaries say every git call is hardened.
findings.scenario: A hostile global git config is exercised against the nine; stop or recreate runs git through a path the sweep never saw.
findings.change: Write 'every romeu command' in both tests, or list the fifteen.

findings.defect: I24 says romeu never extracts archives from memory dirs, and 08 8.5 host half step 2 unbundles git bundles read from the memory dir.
findings.scenario: A reviewer holds romeu salvage against I24 as written and finds it in violation.
findings.change: Write 'never extracts an archive other than a git bundle through gitsafe (bundle verify, unbundle, fsck --strict)'.

findings.defect: The README outline promises 'first run (J1 in six commands)' and J1 has seven steps.
findings.scenario: The README is written to the outline and rule 13 then forces its commands to match a journey with a different count.
findings.change: Say 'the steps of J1'.

findings.defect: A project created later under a retired project's name reads the old project's entries as its own, with the full own-project fields; 05 5.4 has no row for it.
findings.scenario: shop is retired; a new, unrelated shop is created; its sandbox reads a year of the old project's events, ids included.
findings.change: Add a 05 5.4 row, or scope the view by generation or by the project record's creation time.
findings.cost: a row, or a small rule

findings.defect: The section says ROMEU_SETTINGS is the only environment override while locating settings and state by XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME, which are environment overrides.
findings.scenario: A test or a user sets XDG_STATE_HOME and the sentence says nothing happens.
findings.change: Write 'the only romeu-specific environment variable; the XDG variables are honoured'.

findings.defect: The default root $HOME/dev must not be inside a git repository and doctor fails a root inside one; a home directory that is itself a git repository (dotfiles in $HOME) fails the default at J1 step 3 or 4 and init does not say what it does.
findings.scenario: A second adopter with a bare-repo dotfiles setup runs romeu init and then doctor fails on the root it was given by default.
findings.change: Have init detect and refuse with a hint, or say so in J1 step 3.

findings.defect: The manifest is capped at 32 KiB and carries the whole validated run layout and every repo; what happens past the cap (refused at sync, at run, truncated) is unstated.
findings.scenario: A project with twelve repos and a large layout finds out at run, after approval.
findings.change: Say where the cap is checked and with which error id, and make spec validate report it.

findings.defect: No journey builds the dedicated signing agent that signing.agentSocket names (03 3.4, 06 6.4): one key, alive across reboots, and what sync and run say when it is down.
findings.scenario: The operator adds git-ssh-sign to a project and sync exits 2 with RJ-204; the guide for J1 has no step and no recovery for that id.
findings.change: Add a J1 step or a journey for the signing agent (operator steps as preconditions the scenario checks).

findings.defect: Step 5 is described as host checks that can widen a sandbox behind romeu's back and includes VS Code trust (I14, I23), which cannot widen a sandbox; a user with workspace trust disabled cannot run any P command, for a reason the step's own description does not give.
findings.scenario: The refusal is right or wrong; the sentence that justifies it does not cover it, so a reviewer cannot tell.
findings.change: Say the step holds the checks whose failure makes agent output executable on the host, and name trust under that reason.

findings.defect: A2 measures sbx re-prompting for a changed host command and nothing measures the macOS keychain's own ACL prompt when sbx runs security find-generic-password (03 3.4's example) from a non-interactive sbx env run.
findings.scenario: romeu run --no-attach from a script hangs on a keychain dialog nobody sees, or fails; doctor has no row that could warn.
findings.change: Add a keychain observation to A2 (or A1) and, if it prompts, a doctor row or a J1 note on 'always allow'.

findings.defect: romeu run lists exit codes 0-5 and no step of run exits 5 (refused to protect data).
findings.scenario: An implementer adds an exit 5 path to run that nothing in 04 describes, or the generated reference lists a code no path uses.
findings.change: List the exit codes run uses, or name the case that exits 5.

findings.defect: The deferred row fixes that release.yml must not come from the tagged commit, while S1's evidence is 'a ci-run of release.yml on the tagged commit' and GitHub runs a push-tag workflow from the tagged ref; the page does not say how both hold.
findings.scenario: T088 chooses between the two sentences; whichever it picks, one of S1's evidence or the fixed rule is wrong.
findings.change: Say the mechanism now (a workflow_dispatch from main that takes the tag, or a push on main that reads the tag) and phrase S1's evidence to match.

findings.defect: J9 covers a romeu release, a workload bump and a personal kit bump and no journey covers an sbx upgrade on the host (Docker Desktop updates it): gate 1 exits 3 on every project, doctor reports, and 10 10.3 says a floor bump needs a new recording set.
findings.scenario: sbx updates overnight; every romeu run exits 3; the operator approves the toolchain without knowing whether the recordings still describe this sbx.
findings.change: Add an sbx-upgrade path to J9 with what the operator checks and when a re-record is needed.

findings.defect: The snapshot bundle excludes objects reachable from repos[].base, the origin SHAs in refs/romeu/origin, which move only on sync, so after the agent pushes every post-commit snapshot re-bundles already-pushed objects until the next sync; 'the bundle holds only unpushed objects, so it is small' holds only right after a sync.
findings.scenario: A week of commits pushed daily and no sync; each commit rewrites a bundle of the whole week into the memory dir.
findings.change: Refresh base on run as well as sync (a fetch is already in setup), or state the cost.

findings.defect: The ref domain admits invariant ids and probe ids, and no v1 producer writes them except a hand-typed note; a membership set wider than its producers adds concepts the index's 'Simple and explicit' counts.
findings.scenario: A reader asks what event carries I24 as a ref and finds none.
findings.change: Restrict ref to error ids until a producer needs more (an additive version then).

findings.defect: Decision 5 makes the only control over the token a habit (the operator reads the security log at each sitting) whose coverage the record calls unverified; the first principle forbids a mechanism that rests on memory or goodwill, and the collision is not named the way the ADR 0005 collision is.
findings.scenario: The habit lapses after a few sittings and nothing notices; the record reads as if a control exists.
findings.change: Name the collision in Consequences and give the habit a trigger that a tool can see (a dora field for merges by the token, once the two merges can be told apart, as the deferred row says).

findings.defect: The opening says 'the seven decision records under adr/'; there are eight.
findings.scenario: A reader counts and distrusts the other counts.
findings.change: Write eight, or 'the decision records'.

findings.defect: 'What v1 leaves out' says the Deferred decisions table has 28 rows at the commit the plan was written from; the index at this baseline has 36, and the five rows the plan maps to tasks do not include the new ones (release.yml from main, the approval record, the go run escapes once added).
findings.scenario: The plan's mapping of deferred rows to tasks is stale and nobody re-derives it.
findings.change: Re-derive the count and the mapping, or drop the count.

findings.defect: T088 accepts 'release.yml passes tools/ci workflows' under a grammar that forbids the permissions and token the same task's publish, verify and attach steps need (L0-1).
findings.scenario: T088 cannot be completed as written; the grammar is widened inside the task.
findings.change: After L0-1 lands in 10 10.2, make T088's acceptance name the admitted exception and a fixture that fails a second file using it.

findings.defect: Block O3's --require-pass list is the only place that demands results for A2, A3, A5, A6, A9 and A14; the spec's acceptance (10 10.5) does not (L0-18), so the plan covers a gap the spec leaves and the gap returns at any re-probe after O3.
findings.scenario: A5 is re-run alone after a golden change; nothing in the spec requires its new result to be committed.
findings.change: Keep the list and add the spec rule of L0-18; cite it from O3.

findings.defect: T066's J3a acceptance ('starts or reattaches with sbx env run -d') and T019's session table (sessions starting 'stopped') need a recording of sbx env run -d on a stopped sandbox that no block A definition makes (A4 records a stop and a listing).

postmortem: v1.0.0 shipped; a year later the maintainer is the only user, on one of two machines, and the second contributor never came. (1) It shipped late and stale: block B is 90 minutes per host, run twice, and any kit or catalog fix means a new candidate and block B again (11 11.2); two candidates failed on artifacts, each cycle an evening on two laptops, and sbx moved three versions meanwhile so the block A recordings aged (10 10.3; crosses 11 11.2, 10 10.3, 12 12.2, Q7, Q16). (2) The release pipeline could not exist as written: the grammar forbade write permissions and every token (10 10.2) while the release needed both (S1, 12 12.10); the PR that added release.yml loosened the grammar in the same diff under an approval line its author typed and merged with the operator's token (crosses 10 10.2, 05 5.3, 12 12.4, ADR 0008). (3) The security model was a convention in uniform: 'the ruleset requires', 'enforced by' and 'ask-first' (05 5.3, 12 12.4, 12 12.9, ADR 0001 rule 8) rested on a review that no longer existed and a token that could merge, tag and edit rulesets (ADR 0008); the one control was reading the security log, a habit the spec called unverified, which lasted five sittings; the first principle forbids goodwill as a mechanism and the merge gate was exactly that, in four places that still said otherwise (crosses 05 5.4, ADR 0005 rule 1, ADR 0008). (4) Onboarding lost everyone but the author: seven J1 steps, gh with attestations, two verifications, init, doctor (turn VS Code trust on, move the dotfiles repo out of $HOME, remove symlinks into ~/dev), keychain entries, gate 1, a kit diff of thousands of lines, then a ten-minute create under a machine-wide lock; README promised six commands (12 12.8) and S8 excluded everything the user felt (crosses 00 0.2, 04 4.1, S8). (5) 'Nothing lost' was true and useless: salvage proved every byte existed (I17); after the first recreate the dirty-tree commit sat under refs/romeu/salvage where the new clone could not see it, the stash was a ULID-named ref and ignored.tar.gz had no verb; J10 step 3 said raw git on the host clone, which 05 5.4 row 1 warns about; recreates stopped, kit changes became non-events, and .env files travelled into memory dirs and backups on every rm (crosses 00 0.1, 08 8.5, J6, J10, 05 5.4). (6) The ledger recorded and nobody read it: three invariants, a hostile-spool table, a view policy, a probe and two commands (13) for a consumer that was the maintainer reading JSON lines; one lesson cited an event, in month four; S8 was measured on an empty ledger and view derivation grew with the year; the spec's own rule said leave out what the start does not need and ADR 0006 said the maintainer asked (crosses 13, ADR 0005, ADR 0006, 00 0.5, S8). (7) The agent kept moving: Claude Code changed hook payloads and its memory dir; users bumped the workload digest (06 6.2), found julieta pin workload blocked by egress (03 3.5), added the registry by hand, and then the julieta-claude hooks fired into the void and the non-writable memory rule broke startup; Q8 and Q22 were settled once, on one version (crosses 06 6.4, 08 8.2). (8) The daily path said no too often: VS Code trust off (I14 in the preflight), the signing agent not up after a reboot (01 1.5 step 5, for salvage too), sbx auto-updated so gate 1 asked on every project (01 1.4), a .DS_Store in a memory dir (I24); each refusal was correct with a fix hint (crosses 01 1.4, 01 1.5, I14, I24, 06 6.4). (9) Secondary users read the maintainer's setup as the product's: 05 5.4 said the token is today the operator's own; it was about the development sandbox, not sandboxes romeu creates; they concluded romeu forwards your whole GitHub identity and left (crosses 05 5.4, ADR 0008, 06 6.4, 00 0.2). (10) The spec was the product: eight rounds, fourteen pages, eight ADRs, 102 tasks and seven operator blocks for one user before sync existed; 'count concepts' was never applied to the spec; implementers spent their rounds satisfying tools/ci, not asking whether romeu run felt good (crosses the index principles, 12 12.4, 10 10.2, plan.md). (11) The quiet one: writing the spec was more rewarding than using the tool; the rounds were the reward.
lens_critique: Reading with only S1 to S11 measures the spec against targets it wrote for itself, and every one of them is a CI run, a probe on throwaway projects or a document: none is a user outcome, so this reading inherits the criteria's own blind spot and cannot fail the product for a bad first hour, a slow warm run, or a restore that needs raw git. It sees what the criteria do not name (the ledger, the restart path) only as a shape defect, not as a risk; it over-weights consistency (two states of one sentence) relative to design risk because consistency is what a text alone can prove; and it cannot weigh any sbx fact without a host. It is good at finding where the spec contradicts itself and weak at saying whether the thing it describes would be worth using.
missing_viewpoint: The human at the gate prompt: the approver at a TTY who must read a ten-thousand-line kit diff, a secret's argv and a capability set and type y, and whose attention is the one control every security claim collapses onto (gate 2, the approval line, the security-log habit); no lens models approval fatigue or the cost of a wrong y. Close seconds: the platform vendor's view (what sbx, BuildKit and macOS actually do, which L15 covers as churn and not as present behaviour) and the person who does the restore after a loss, which L4 covers only up to the loss.
